chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Fellow patients and Pickin' Joe Steele's rapid tap
summary: Patients included Bud Powell and a saxophonist; Green recalls tap dancer Joe Steele, who developed Little Buck and Arthur Duncan, and demonstrates his rapid tap.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Who were some of the other patients that were performing?
Yes. Pickin' John Steele, you know -- Bud Powell, and some gentleman from the Ted Rayburn Orchestra, an alto saxophone player -- I think he name was Ross.
Pickin' John Steele -- what kind of tap dancing did he do?
Oh, he was very versatile. He did -- he did like rapid tap, you see. That's supposed to have been
one of the speed tap dances, see. And he developed people like Little Buck, Arthur Duncan -- he put them on the road to the profession, you see.
Can you do his style of tap dancing -- Pickin' John Steele?
No, no, no. I could do a step that he taught me, yes, I could do that.
Yes, I'd like for you to see it also, so I'm going to beat my -- I'd be glad to have the pleasure to do it now.
Okay, here we go. This is Pickin' -- Joe Steele or John Steele?
That's Pickin' Joe Steele and the rapid tap.
(unintelligible) Here we go again. Let's see.
